Senses.Explanation: To disdain becoming a buddha and refuse to do it: a phrase used in warning, criticism, praise, and description of an assembly. Senses.Explanation: To turn one’s back on awareness and join with sensory dust is to follow appearances until they govern one’s response. Pu’an contrasts nominal teaching with clear seeing and calls the former a turn toward dust. Tianyin connects the turn with clinging and repeated pursuit. Fenyang says people who dispute surface matters and fail to examine their source make this turn. Hongzhi says it places one within the condition of ordinary beings rather than the unobstructed field he has just described. Linquan applies the phrase to a person who does not recognize what is already present and instead chases things. Muyun says daily life can hide the great scripture in plain sight when people turn toward dust. Ruibai gives the clearest contrast: losing sight of what is already present is this turn, while recognizing it is a turn back from dust.

AlternateTargets: Neither recoil nor contact will do; it is like a heap of fire
SearchAliases: turning away touching both wrong great mass of fire
Senses.Note: The Mirror Samadhi line says that turning away and touching are both wrong, like approaching a great mass of fire. Shiyu quotes it while warning against settling on pristine purity; Yuanjie brings it into an account of a local teacher’s transmission; Suru uses it to close a question about what remains after all possessions are cast off; Tianru extends the fire image to show why both taking and rejecting fail; Yongjue explains that turning toward burns and turning away is no answer. The image is a warning about fixing a stance, not a recipe for avoiding the fire.

Senses.Explanation: “Turning away and touching are both wrong, as with a great mass of fire” leaves no safe fixed stance to take. Shiyu warns against clinging to spotless purity; Yuanjie invokes the line in a transmission address; Suru uses it after asking what remains once all is cast off. Tianru extends the fire image to taking and rejecting, while Yongjue explains why neither side of the dilemma is a refuge.
